name: Halwa Puri
description: Traditional Pakistani breakfast of semolina halwa, spiced chickpeas and freshly fried puffed puris.
ingredients: ½ tsp salt for puri dough
method: For the halwa, heat ghee and roast the semolina over medium-low heat until fragrant and lightly golden. Separately dissolve the sugar in about 1½ cups hot water with cardamom.
Carefully add the hot sugar liquid to the roasted semolina while stirring. Cook on low heat until the liquid is absorbed and the halwa becomes glossy.
For the chickpeas, heat a little oil, add chana masala and the cooked chickpeas with a splash of water, then simmer until well seasoned. Adjust salt to taste.
For the puris, mix flour and salt and add water gradually to make a firm but pliable dough. Rest covered for about 15 minutes.
Divide the dough into small balls and roll into thin discs, keeping unused dough covered.
Heat frying oil over medium-high heat. Slide in one puri at a time, gently press with a slotted spoon until it puffs, turn, and fry until lightly golden. Drain well.
Serve the hot puris immediately with halwa and chickpea curry.
tips: Roast semolina before adding liquid for better flavour and texture.
Puri dough should be firmer than chapati dough; very soft dough absorbs more oil.
Use properly hot oil so puris puff quickly without becoming greasy.
storage: Halwa and chickpea curry can be refrigerated covered for up to 2 days. Puris are best freshly fried.
